body:
## Pull request overview

This PR upgrades `RecordPickerDialog` and `LookupField` in `@object-ui/fields` to support schema-driven base filters (`lookup_filters`), type-aware cell formatting, pluggable FilterUI/ObjectGrid integration via render slots, and column resizing for the built-in table fallback.

**Changes:**
- Add `lookupFilters`, `cellRenderer`, `filterColumns`, `renderFilterBar`, and `renderGrid` capabilities to `RecordPickerDialog`, including filter injection into `DataSource.find()`.
- Add a bridge module to break the `index.tsx` ↔ `RecordPickerDialog` circular dependency for `getCellRenderer`.
- Extend `LookupField` to pass `lookup_filters`, derived filter columns, and the bridged `cellRenderer` into `RecordPickerDialog`, plus add comprehensive tests.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 9 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/_cell-renderer-bridge.ts | Adds singleton bridge to share `getCellRenderer` without circular imports. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/RecordPickerDialog.tsx | Implements lookup filter injection, filter bar + slots, cell formatting hook, and resize handles. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx | Passes `lookup_filters` through and derives filter columns/cell renderer for the picker dialog. |
| packages/fields/src/record-picker.test.tsx | Adds test coverage for new RecordPicker features (filters, slots, formatting, resize). |
| packages/fields/src/index.tsx | Registers the cell renderer resolver into the bridge at module init. |
</details>

For the built-in `select` filter input, `onValueChange` passes the Radix Select string value directly into `filterValues`. This loses the original option type (e.g., number/boolean) and makes it impossible to support object option values. Consider storing a stable primitive key in state and converting it back to the original typed value (or limiting Select options to string-only values) before generating `$filter`.

Inline `style={styleWidth}` is used to apply per-column widths during resize. This conflicts with the repo’s “no inline styles” guidance (.github/copilot-instructions.md) and also makes it harder to theme/override. Consider switching to a CSS-variable based scheme (e.g., `--col-name-width`) with Tailwind classes, or delegating resizing to `renderGrid` (ObjectGrid) which can own the styling implementation.

`mapFieldTypeToFilterType` maps `select`/`status` to a `select` filter input, but `LookupField` doesn’t provide `options` when deriving `filterColumns` from `lookup_columns`. This results in an empty Select in the built-in filter bar. Consider either excluding `select`/`status` from the auto-derived filter columns (falling back to text input), or extending the metadata so options can be supplied.

The `setCellRendererResolver` import is placed mid-file after executable statements. While valid ESM, it’s inconsistent with typical import organization and can be easy to miss when scanning the module for dependencies/side effects. Consider moving this import to the top-level import section and keeping the resolver registration near other initialization side effects.

`mergedFilter` combines `lookupFilters` and user-entered filter-bar values via object spread (`{ ...baseFilter, ...userFilter }`). This allows user filters to override base `lookupFilters`, which are documented as “restricts which records are selectable”. Consider ensuring base filters always win (e.g., merge order reversed) or combine them in a non-overridable way (e.g., an explicit AND structure if supported) so users can’t loosen the restriction by filtering on the same field.

`SelectItem` uses `String(opt.value)` for both `key` and `value`. If options contain non-unique values once stringified (especially objects) this can lead to React key collisions and incorrect selection behavior. Consider requiring primitive option values and/or using a dedicated stable `id`/`valueKey` for the Select value.

`handleResizeStart` registers `document`-level mousemove/mouseup listeners but only removes them on mouseup. If the dialog unmounts/closes mid-drag, those listeners can remain attached and may attempt to call `setColumnWidths` on an unmounted component. Add an unmount/close cleanup path that removes any active listeners (or use an AbortController / pointer events with capture + cleanup).

This introduces inline styles (`style={...}`) for table layout. The repo’s styling guidance forbids inline styles in favor of Tailwind utilities (see .github/copilot-instructions.md). If dynamic layout is required, consider a Tailwind-based approach (e.g., toggling `table-fixed`) and/or CSS variables with predefined classes, or rely on the injected `renderGrid` implementation for resizing.

The auto-generated `options` for filter columns can include non-primitive values (objects), but the built-in Select later stringifies option values/keys. For object values this becomes "[object Object]" (often non-unique) and can’t be reliably mapped back to the original value when building `$filter`. It’d be safer to only generate options for primitive values (string/number/boolean) or generate a stable primitive key (e.g., id) and map back when applying the filter.
